rd: おはよう ございます
lit: おはよう (early) ございます (polite 'is')
use: Morning greeting, used until about late morning. Use it with coworkers, teachers, neighbours; with friends and family drop ございます.
All-purpose daytime hello, roughly 10am to dusk. Safe with anyone; a bit stiff among close friends.

lit: 今晩 (this evening) は (topic marker, read 'wa') ...
use: Greeting from dusk onward, when meeting someone. Not used when leaving (that is おやすみなさい).

lit: お休み (rest) なさい (please do)
use: Said before going to bed or when parting late at night. Never used as a daytime hello.

lit: さようなら (if that is how it is...)
use: A fairly final goodbye, common at school and in formal settings. In daily life friends usually say じゃあね or またね instead.
Casual goodbye between friends and family. Very common in anime and daily talk.
Friendly goodbye when you expect to meet again. Add a time for precision: また明日 (see you tomorrow).

rd: おひさしぶり です
lit: お久しぶり (long time) です (is)
use: Greeting someone you have not seen in a long while. Politeness adjusts by dropping です with friends.
alt: お久しぶりですね (polite, with 'isn't it')

en: How are you? / Are you well?
lit: お元気 (healthy, honorific) です (is) か (question)
use: Asked of someone you have not seen for a while, not as a daily hello. Reply 元気です.
Standard answer to お元気ですか. Add おかげさまで (thanks to you) to be extra polite.
Said when leaving home, school, or the office, meaning 'I'll go and come back'. The reply is いってらっしゃい.

en: Have a good day / See you later (to someone leaving)
lit: 行って (go) らっしゃい (honorific 'come')
use: Reply to いってきます, said by whoever stays behind. Warm and routine; used with family and colleagues.

jp: あけましておめでとうございます
rd: あけまして おめでとう ございます
lit: あけまして (opening [of the new year]) おめでとう (congratulations) ございます (polite)
use: Said from January 1 for the first days of the year. Before the New Year people say 良いお年を (have a good year).

rd: おたんじょうび おめでとう
lit: お誕生日 (birthday) おめでとう (congratulations)
use: Say it to friends and family on their birthday. Add ございます to be polite to a boss or older person.
alt: お誕生日おめでとうございます (polite)

use: For any good news: passing an exam, marriage, a baby, a win. Add ございます for polite use.
alt: おめでとうございます (polite)

jp: ありがとうございます
rd: ありがとう ございます
lit: ありがとう (thanks) ございます (polite 'is')
use: The standard polite thanks, fine with anyone. Use the past ございました after something is finished.
alt: どうもありがとうございます (very polite)
ありがとうございました (polite, past)

jp: どうも ありがとうございました
rd: どうも ありがとう ございました
en: Thank you very much (for what you did)
lit: どうも (very much) ありがとう (thanks) ございました (polite, past)
use: Use after receiving help or service, especially when leaving a shop or ending a favour. Warm and slightly formal.

rd: どう いたしまして
lit: どう (how) いたしまして (doing, humble)
use: Reply to thanks. Japanese often just say いえいえ (no no) or 気にしないで instead, as this can sound a little stiff.

en: Excuse me / Sorry / Thank you (for the trouble)
use: The most useful word: get a waiter's attention, apologise lightly, squeeze past someone, or thank someone for going to trouble. Polite and flexible.

lit: ごめん (pardon) なさい (please do)
use: A sincere personal apology to people close to you, or for a minor mistake. Stronger and more personal than すみません.

rd: もうしわけ ありません
lit: 申し訳 (excuse) ありません (there is none)
use: Business and customer-service apology, used to superiors and customers. Literally 'I have no excuse'.
alt: 申し訳ございません (even more formal)

use: Said when entering a room, leaving a meeting, or hanging up a call. Part of workplace and school manners.
alt: 失礼しました (I apologise for what I did, past)

use: Attach it after a noun to ask for something: 水をお願いします. It is the polite 'please' for service situations.

en: Please go ahead / Here you are
use: Offering something or permission: gesturing someone to go first, handing something over, inviting someone to sit.
A short mumbled thanks, hello or apology. Casual and polite-neutral; fine to shop assistants and neighbours.
alt: どうもすみません (sorry, more polite)

jp: 気にしないでください
rd: きに しないで ください
lit: 気 (mind) に しないで (not doing) ください (please)
use: Reassuring someone who apologised or feels they troubled you. Use the short form 気にしないで with friends.
alt: 気にしなくていいよ (casual, 'no need to worry')

rd: だいじょうぶ です
en: I'm fine / It's OK / No thank you
use: Works both as 'I'm OK' and as a polite refusal ('No, I'm fine, thanks'). Tone and context tell which.

rd: おまたせ しました
lit: お待たせ (making [you] wait) しました (did)
use: Say it when you arrive late, or when bringing food or finishing something people waited for.
Offering someone to go through a door or in a line before you. Also said at the elevator.
Say it when you step into someone's house. When leaving: お邪魔しました.
Yes, and also 'I hear you' or 'here' when your name is called. Polite and universal; it does not always mean agreement.
The polite 'no', also used to deflect compliments or thanks. Japanese often soften it or use ちょっと….
Casual yes among friends and family. Do not use it to teachers, bosses, or strangers; use はい.
Casual no, said with falling or flat intonation, in contrast to うん (yes) with a rising feel. Friends only.

lit: そう (that way) です (is) か (question)
use: Reaction to new information, said with falling pitch to show you took it in. Rising pitch makes it sound like genuine doubt.

lit: そう (that way) です (is) ね (isn't it)
use: Agree with the speaker, or buy time to think before answering. Casual: そうだね.
Express surprise or ask for confirmation. Casual version is 本当? or ほんとに?.
Signals that you understand a reasoning or explanation. Slightly 'know-it-all' to superiors; use なるほどですね or そうですか then.

lit: わかり (understand) ました (did, polite past)
use: Say it after instructions or requests to show you understood and will do it. Casual: わかった.
alt: かしこまりました (very polite, service)

use: Giving permission or accepting an offer. With a flat tone it may also mean 'no need, thanks'.

en: That's no good / You can't / Not allowed
use: Refusing permission or saying something is not OK. Casual だめ! is common to children.
Strong agreement or yes. Add です to be polite: もちろんです.
Use when you are not sure. Combine with だと思う (I think) or でしょう to soften.
A filler word while thinking. Also あの, ええと. Helps you sound natural when forming a sentence.

lit: そう (that way) だ (is) ね (isn't it)
use: Casual agreement with a friend. Also used to stall for a moment.
Show you agree with a point just made. Very common in everyday conversations and anime.
Agree with someone and invite them to agree. Casual: だよね.
A small reaction of mild surprise or interest while someone talks. Very frequent in conversation.
Praise or astonishment, for people, skills, food, scenery. One of the most common reactions in anime.
Casual 'no' to correct or disagree, also a starting 'well, actually'. In anime it can be stronger: 'No!'.
alt: いやいや (no no, waving it off)

use: Brief confirmation among friends and coworkers in chat. Not polite enough for a boss.

en: I don't understand / I don't know
use: Your most important survival phrase. Say it plainly when you did not catch something. Casual: わからない.
alt: よくわかりません (I don't quite understand)

jp: もう一度お願いします
rd: もう いちど おねがい します
lit: もう (more) 一度 (one time) お願いします (I request)
use: Ask someone to repeat what they said. Natural and polite in conversation, shops and stations.
alt: もう一度言ってください (polite)

jp: ゆっくりお願いします
rd: ゆっくり おねがい します
lit: ゆっくり (slowly) お願いします (I request)
use: Ask a speaker to slow down. Combine with もう一度: もう一度、ゆっくりお願いします.
alt: ゆっくり話してください (please speak slowly)

rd: これ は なん ですか
lit: これ (this) は (topic) 何 (what) です (is) か (question)
use: Point at something and ask. Swap これ for それ (that near you) or あれ (that over there).
alt: それは何ですか (what is that?)

jp: 日本語で何と言いますか
rd: にほんご で なんと いいます か
en: How do you say this in Japanese?
lit: 日本語 (Japanese) で (in) 何と (what) 言います (say) か (question)
use: Use it with pointing or an English word to learn vocab on the spot. Reverse: 英語で何ですか (what is it in English?).
alt: これは日本語で何ですか (this, in Japanese?)

rd: どういう いみ ですか
lit: どういう (what kind of) 意味 (meaning) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask about a word you heard. Put the word first: 「大丈夫」はどういう意味ですか.

jp: 日本語が少し話せます
rd: にほんご が すこし はなせます
en: I can speak a little Japanese
lit: 日本語 (Japanese) が (subject) 少し (a little) 話せます (can speak)
use: Set expectations; people will then speak more simply. Use 少しだけ to stress 'just a bit'.
alt: 日本語が下手です (my Japanese is bad)
日本語を勉強しています (I'm studying Japanese)

rd: えいご が はなせます か
lit: 英語 (English) が (subject) 話せます (can speak) か (question)
use: Ask before launching into English, at a hotel or shop. Smile and add すみません first.
alt: 英語わかりますか (do you understand English?)

lit: 聞こえ (be audible) ません (not)
use: On a noisy street or a bad phone line. Add もう少し大きい声でお願いします (a bit louder, please).
Ask someone to write a word, price, or address when speaking is too hard.

jp: ちょっと待ってください
rd: ちょっと まって ください
lit: ちょっと (a little) 待って (wait) ください (please)
use: Buy time to think or look something up. Close friends hear ちょっと待って.
alt: 少々お待ちください (formal, service)

rd: たすけて ください
use: For real trouble. For small favours use 手伝ってください (please lend a hand).
alt: 手伝ってください (please help with a task)

use: About facts, people, places you are not aware of. Different from わかりません (can't grasp/figure out).
alt: 知らなかった (I didn't know)

use: Use it for words, names, items left behind. 忘れ物 means a lost item.

lit: 迷い (lose one's way) ました (did)
use: Say it when asking for directions: 道に迷いました (I lost my way).
alt: 道に迷いました (I lost my way)

en: I'm in trouble / I have a problem
lit: 困って (be troubled) います (am doing)
use: Explain you need help before describing the problem. Common at counters and with staff.

rd: てつだって ください
lit: 手伝って (assist) ください (please)
use: Ask for hands-on help: carrying, filling in a form. Less dramatic than 助けて.
alt: 手伝いましょうか (shall I help?)

use: Basic question. Before です/の/か, 何 reads 'nan'; before other words it can read 'nani' (何を, 何が).
Ask about a person. Polite form of who is どなた.
Put a place first: トイレはどこですか. Also ask 'where' to point: どこ?.
About events and plans: 試験はいつですか (when is the exam?).
alt: いつ行く? (casual, when will you go?)

use: Asks for a reason, can sound sympathetic or surprised. Answer with から (because).
Everyday casual 'why'. In anime often angry or incredulous: なんでだ!
Ask for a method: どうやって行きますか (how do I get there?).
alt: どうすればいい? (casual, 'what should I do?')

lit: いくつ (how many) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask for a count of items. With people's ages use おいくつですか; to ask for number use 何個.

lit: どれ (which one of three or more) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask to identify something among several. For two, どちら is common; to say 'which + noun' use どの.

rd: どう おもいます か
lit: どう (how) 思います (think) か (question)
use: Ask for someone's opinion. Casual: どう思う?.

lit: どう (how) した (did) の (soft question)
use: To someone who looks troubled or acts strangely. Warm and caring, among close people.

rd: なに してる の
lit: 何 (what) してる (doing) の (soft question)
use: Casual chat starter, or asking what someone is up to. Polite: 何をしていますか.

lit: 何時 (what time) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask for the time, or a schedule: 電車は何時ですか (what time is the train?).

rd: なにが すき ですか
lit: 何 (what) が (subject) 好き (liked) です (is) か (question)
use: Good conversation opener. Replace 何 with a category: 食べ物は何が好きですか.
alt: 趣味は何ですか (what's your hobby?)

rd: どこ から きました か
en: Where are you from? / Where did you come from?
lit: どこ (where) から (from) 来ました (came) か (question)
use: Ask where someone is from. Answer: アメリカから来ました.
alt: お国はどちらですか (very polite)
どこの出身ですか (where are you from?)

en: How is it? / How about it?
use: Ask for impressions or offer a suggestion: コーヒーはどうですか (how about coffee?).
Express happiness about something that happened to you. Polite: うれしいです.
For activities, events or time together. Past: 楽しかった (it was fun).
Sadness over losses or sad news. Related: さびしい (lonely).
Say after work or exercise. Polite: 疲れました.

rd: おなか が すいた
lit: お腹 (stomach) が (subject) すいた (became empty)
use: Very common. Polite: お腹がすきました. Another casual word: はらへった (rough, male).
alt: お腹ペコペコ (very hungry, casual)

rd: のど が かわいた
lit: のど (throat) が (subject) 渇いた (dried)
use: Say when you want a drink. Polite: のどが渇きました.
Used about yourself or others. Add です for polite use.
Both 'I'm scared' and 'that's scary'. Context tells which. Polite: 怖いです.

en: I like it / I like you
use: Expresses liking: [thing] が好きです. Alone to a person, it means romantic confession.

en: I love it / I really like it
use: Strong liking for foods, hobbies, friends. 大好きです is polite.
alt: 愛してる (I love you, rare, deep)

en: I hate it / I dislike it
use: Strong dislike. Softer: あまり好きじゃない (don't like it much).
alt: あまり好きじゃない (don't much like it)

en: I don't want to / I hate that
use: Express refusal or aversion. Childish or strong in tone. Anime uses いやだ!
For weather and room temperature. Hot thing/touch uses 熱い, same sound.
alt: 暑いですね (it's hot, isn't it)

use: Weather small talk. 'Cold' to the touch is 冷たい.
alt: 寒いですね (it's cold, isn't it)

use: Pain. Specify where: お腹が痛い (my stomach hurts), 頭が痛い (my head hurts).
alt: 頭が痛い (I have a headache)

use: Shyness or embarrassment. Common in anime romance and comedy.
Before exams, interviews, speeches. Past: 緊張した.
alt: ドキドキする (my heart's pounding)

lit: 楽しみ (something to look forward to)
use: Say it when anticipating an event: 明日が楽しみ (I'm looking forward to tomorrow).
alt: 楽しみにしています (polite, 'I'm looking forward')

use: Loneliness or missing someone. Often used when a friend leaves.

en: I was surprised / You scared me
use: Mild shock. Polite: びっくりしました.
Praise a film, joke, or idea. Opposite is つまらない (boring).
Praise food. Say おいしいです to be polite. Even more: すごくおいしい.
Used for babies, animals, clothes, people. Very common in Japanese. Strong form: めっちゃかわいい.
Praise people, cars, moves, anime heroes. Polite: かっこいいですね.
Say it about a meal, a day, a trip. Equivalent to 'it's the best'.
Explain you have no time. Polite: 忙しいです.
Hot baths, fresh air, massage. Casual and fun.

rd: これ を ください
lit: これ (this) を (object) ください (please give)
use: Point and say it to order or buy. Swap これ for any noun: 水をください.
alt: これお願いします (this, please)

lit: いくら (how much) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask a price while pointing: これはいくらですか. Prices are given in 円 (en).
Comment on a price: ちょっと高い (a bit expensive). Opposite is 安い (cheap).
alt: ちょっと高いです (it's a bit pricey)

use: Praise a good price: 安い! Opposite is 高い (expensive).

rd: おかいけい おねがい します
lit: お会計 (bill) お願いします (I request)
use: Say it in a restaurant after you have finished eating. Staff will bring the bill or point to the register.
alt: お勘定お願いします (older style)
チェックお願いします (casual, English-loan)

rd: カード は つかえます か
lit: カード (card) は (topic) 使えます (can use) か (question)
use: Ask before paying at small shops and restaurants. Many accept only cash.
alt: クレジットカードは使えますか (credit card?)

rd: ふくろ は いりません
lit: 袋 (bag) は (topic) いりません (don't need)
use: Say it at a convenience store or supermarket where bags cost extra and the clerk asks.
alt: 袋は大丈夫です (the bag is fine)

jp: メニューをお願いします
rd: メニュー を おねがい します
lit: メニュー (menu) を (object) お願いします (I request)
use: Say it after being seated. For English menus: 英語のメニューはありますか.
alt: 英語のメニューはありますか (English menu?)

rd: おすすめ は なん ですか
lit: おすすめ (recommendation) は (topic) 何 (what) ですか (is?)
use: Ask the staff what is good; helpful when you cannot read a menu.
alt: おすすめはありますか (do you have recommendations?)

rd: みず を ください
lit: 水 (water) を (object) ください (please give)
use: Water is free in most restaurants and will be brought. The お冷 (ohiya) is cold water.

rd: ちゅうもん おねがい します
lit: 注文 (order) お願いします (I request)
use: Call a waiter over by saying すみません first, then this. Or press the call button on the table.
alt: すみません、注文いいですか (excuse me, can I order?)

lit: ひとつ (one thing) ください (please give)
use: Counting items by pointing: ふたつ (2), みっつ (3). Combine: これをふたつください.
alt: これを二つお願いします (two of these)

en: Let's eat / Thanks for the meal (before eating)
lit: いただき (receive, humble) ます (polite)
use: Said by everyone before eating, with hands together. It thanks the cook and the food itself. Always say it.

rd: ごちそう さま でした
en: Thank you for the meal (after eating)
lit: ごちそう (feast) さま (honorific) でした (was)
use: Said after eating, and to the staff when leaving a restaurant. Casual: ごちそうさま.
alt: ごちそうさまです (said when someone treats you)

use: Praise after a meal. Polite: おいしかったです. A real compliment to a host or cook.
alt: すごくおいしかった (it was really good)

rd: みている だけ です
lit: 見ている (looking) だけ (only) です (is)
use: Politely decline a shop assistant's offer to help. Often accompanied by a small bow.

jp: 試着してもいいですか
rd: しちゃく しても いい ですか
ro: shichaku shite mo ii desu ka
lit: 試着 (try on) して (do) も (even) いい (OK) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask in clothing stores. You will be pointed to the fitting room.
alt: 試着できますか (can I try it on?)

jp: おかわりお願いします
rd: おかわり おねがい します
lit: おかわり (refill) お願いします (I request)
use: Used for rice, tea, coffee, or drinks when you want a refill. Some places refill rice free.
alt: おかわりください (please give a refill)

use: Say the number of people when you enter a restaurant. 一人 (hitori) for one, 三人 (sannin) for three.

lit: いらっしゃいませ (honorific 'please come')
use: You hear it on entering shops and restaurants. You do not need to reply, just nod.

jp: 持ち帰りでお願いします
rd: もちかえり で おねがい します
lit: 持ち帰り (takeaway) で (as) お願いします (I request)
use: For takeout. For dining in, you say ここで食べます (I'll eat here).

rd: トイレ は どこ ですか
lit: トイレ (toilet) は (topic) どこ (where) です (is) か (question)
use: Probably the most useful travel sentence. Also works with お手洗い (otearai) in polite contexts.
alt: お手洗いはどこですか (more polite)

rd: えき は どこ ですか
lit: 駅 (station) は (topic) どこ (where) です (is) か (question)
use: Replace 駅 with another place: コンビニ, ホテル, 出口.
alt: 一番近い駅はどこですか (where is the nearest station?)

rd: 〜 に いきたい です
lit: 〜 (place) に (to) 行きたい (want to go) です (is)
use: Tell a taxi driver, station staff or a friend where you want to go: 京都に行きたいです.
Direction word. With 行きます: まっすぐ行ってください (go straight).
alt: まっすぐ行ってください (go straight)

use: Used in directions: 右に曲がってください (please turn right). 曲がる means to turn.
alt: 右に曲がってください (turn right)
左に曲がってください (turn left)

use: Ask whether a place is near. Opposite question: 遠いですか (is it far?).
alt: ここから遠いですか (is it far from here?)

jp: この電車は〜に行きますか
rd: この でんしゃ は 〜 に いきます か
ro: kono densha wa ~ ni ikimasu ka
lit: この (this) 電車 (train) は (topic) 〜に (to) 行きます (go) か (question)
use: Check before boarding. Replace 電車 with バス (bus).
alt: このバスは〜に行きますか (does this bus go to ~?)

rd: なんばんせん ですか
lit: 何番線 (which platform) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask station staff or a passer-by for the platform number.

rd: 〜 まで いくら ですか
lit: 〜 (place) まで (up to) いくら (how much) です (is) か (question)
use: Used for train tickets or taxi fares. 駅までいくらですか.
alt: 〜までお願いします (to ~, please, to a taxi)

rd: ここ は どこ ですか
en: Where am I? / Where is this?
lit: ここ (here) は (topic) どこ (where) です (is) か (question)
use: When you are lost. Show a map and ask これはどこですか (where is this?).
alt: 今どこですか (where am I now?)

jp: 乗り換えはどこですか
rd: のりかえ は どこ ですか
lit: 乗り換え (transfer) は (topic) どこ (where) です (is) か (question)
use: Used in big stations. Staff will point to the correct platform or line.
alt: 乗り換えが必要ですか (do I need to transfer?)

rd: あるいて なんぷん ですか
lit: 歩いて (walking) 何分 (how many minutes) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask how long on foot: 駅から歩いて何分ですか.
alt: 何分かかりますか (how long does it take?)
電車で何分ですか (how many minutes by train?)

jp: ここで止めてください
rd: ここ で とめて ください
lit: ここ (here) で (at) 止めて (stop) ください (please)
use: Tell a taxi driver where to stop. Taxi doors open automatically.
alt: ここでお願いします (here, please)

jp: 写真を撮ってもいいですか
rd: しゃしん を とって も いい ですか
ro: shashin o totte mo ii desu ka
lit: 写真 (photo) を (object) 撮って (take) も (even) いい (OK) です (is) か (question)
use: Ask before photographing people, shops, or shrines. Also: 写真を撮ってもらえますか (could you take a photo of us?).
alt: 写真を撮ってください (please take a photo)
撮ってもいいですか (May I take one?)

use: At immigration or hotel check-in, hand over your passport and say this.
alt: パスポートをお願いします (staff asks for it)

rd: よやく して います
lit: 予約 (reservation) して (do) います (am)
use: Say it at hotels or restaurants. Add the name: 田中で予約しています.

rd: いりぐち ・ でぐち
use: Signs in stations, shops, and buildings. Useful to ask 出口はどこですか.
alt: 出口はどこですか (where is the exit?)

lit: 初めまして (for the first time)
use: The standard opener when meeting someone for the first time. Follow with your name and よろしくお願いします.

rd: わたし の なまえ は 〜 です
lit: 私 (I) の (possessive) 名前 (name) は (topic) 〜です (is)
use: Self-introduction. Shortened: 〜です, or 〜と申します (formal, humble).

jp: よろしくお願いします
rd: よろしく おねがい します
en: Please treat me well / Nice to meet you
lit: よろしく (well) お願いします (I request)
use: Used after introductions, and when asking for a favour or beginning a collaboration. Casual: よろしく.
alt: どうぞよろしくお願いします (very polite)

use: Tell where you are from: アメリカから来ました.
Self introduction. Replace with your job: 会社員です (office worker), エンジニアです.
alt: 会社員です (I'm an office worker)

rd: しゅみ は なん ですか
lit: 趣味 (hobby) は (topic) 何 (what) です (is) か (question)
use: Safe small talk with new acquaintances. Answer: 趣味は〜です.
Casual invitation to go together. Polite: 行きましょう.
Said to someone leaving or doing something risky. Polite: 気をつけてください.

en: Take care of yourself (when parting for long)
use: For long separations, such as a friend moving away. Feels slightly final and warm.
Said when raising drinks together. Everyone waits until all have a glass, then toasts.

en: Get well soon / Take care of yourself
use: To someone sick or injured. Used by shopkeepers, doctors and friends.
alt: お大事にしてください (polite)

rd: おさき に しつれい します
en: Excuse me for leaving before you
lit: お先に (ahead) 失礼 (rudeness) します (do)
use: Said when leaving work before others. Coworkers reply お疲れ様でした.

en: Did you wait? / Sorry I'm late
use: Casual question when you meet someone you kept waiting. Reply: ううん、今来たところ (no, I just got here).
alt: 待たせてごめん (sorry to make you wait)
ううん、今来たところ (no, I just arrived)

lit: 今度 (next time) 遊ぼう (let's play)
use: Friendly invitation, often vague. It may not lead to a real plan.
alt: また遊ぼうね (let's hang out again)

use: Show agreement. Casual: 私も! Men may say 俺も.

rd: いっしょ に どう ですか
en: Would you like to join me?
lit: 一緒に (together) どう (how) です (is) か (question)
use: Invite someone politely: 一緒にご飯はどうですか (how about eating together?).
alt: 一緒に行きませんか (won't you go with me?)

use: Say at the end of a party or outing. Polite: 楽しかったです.
alt: 楽しかったね (it was fun, wasn't it?)

rd: おねがい が あります
en: I have a favour to ask
lit: お願い (request) が (subject) あります (exists)
use: Prepare a request politely before saying it. Casual: お願いがあるんだけど.
alt: お願いがあるんだけど (casual)
ちょっといいですか (do you have a minute?)

use: Said to make someone stop doing something. Add ください for polite; やめろ is a harsh command.
Calling out to stop someone leaving or to get a moment. Polite: 待ってください.
alt: ちょっと待って (wait a sec)

use: Asked with rising intonation when someone looks hurt or upset. Reply 大丈夫 (I'm okay). Polite: 大丈夫ですか.
Shock reaction to surprising news. Literally 'lie', used like 'no way!'. Noun for lying: うそつき.
alt: うそでしょ (you've got to be kidding)

use: Disbelief at something unexpected or feared. Anime characters say it when the villain's identity or plan is revealed.
Self-motivation or confirming a plan. Hero announces readiness. Often before action.
alt: よっしゃ (more fired-up, Kansai flavour)

use: Battle cry or a push to move out. ぞ gives a rough, masculine, emphatic tone.
Confident reassurance that you will handle it. 任せろ is a rougher male version.
alt: 俺に任せろ (leave it to me, male)

use: Used by heroes and in emotional scenes. Also 信じてる (I trust you).
alt: 信じてる (I believe in you)

use: An urgent cry for help. A staple in anime and dramas. Real emergencies: 助けて!

en: Don't mess with me! / Quit joking!
lit: ふざける (to joke around) な (don't)
use: Angry shout, very rough. Never use to someone you respect. Common from villains and angry heroes.
alt: 冗談じゃない (this is no joke)

use: Angry or shocked, masculine and confrontational. Very common in anime.
alt: 何を言ってる (what are you saying?)
なんだって? (what did you say?)

en: Damn! / Oh no, I messed up
lit: しまった (ended, I blew it)
use: Realising a mistake or something bad. Related to しまう (finish up); often said under the breath.
alt: やっちゃった (oops, I did it)

en: What do you mean? / What's going on?
lit: どういう (what kind of) こと (thing)
use: Demand an explanation after a shock. Polite: どういうことですか.
alt: どういう意味? (what does that mean?)

lit: 頑張って (try hard, request form)
use: Encouragement to someone about to do something hard. Add ください for politeness. To someone already exhausted, avoid it; use 無理しないで.
alt: 頑張ります (I'll do my best)

en: Good work / Thanks for your effort
use: Greeting between coworkers and teammates: for end-of-day, after work or tasks. Formal: お疲れ様でした.
Said when arriving home or back to the office. Reply is おかえり.
alt: ただいま戻りました (formal, office)

use: Reply to ただいま. Polite: おかえりなさい.
Joy at success or good news. Said alone or loudly.
Urgent order from heroes or rescuers. Polite request: 逃げてください.
Shout when danger is near. Also describes something risky.
Draw attention to something. Polite: 見てください. 見ろ is a rough command.
Used to get someone to hear you out, often emotionally: 聞いてくれ (male).
Telling others to quiet down. Polite: 静かにしてください.
Used by police or captors. The 'verb + な' pattern is a rough prohibition.
Anger and revenge in dramas and anime. Strong; often a villain or hero vow.
alt: 絶対に許さない (I'll never forgive you)

use: Declaration of determination, rival-style. Opposite 負けた (I lost).
alt: 絶対負けない (I'll never lose)

use: Emphasis word. 絶対に行く (I will definitely go), 絶対ダメ (absolutely not).
alt: 絶対に (with に, more emphasis)

use: Seal a promise. Popular in emotional scenes. Pinky promise: 指切り.
Optimism in a tough spot. Said by friendly characters.
alt: なんとかなるさ (it'll be alright)
なんとかする (I'll manage it)

use: Resignation, accepting what cannot be changed. Very Japanese attitude.
Slang with many meanings: danger, shock, or super-good, depending on context. Casual only; avoid at work.
Complain about a bad situation. Opposite 最高 (the best).
Rough curse of frustration, very common in anime. Do not use in polite company.
Check that someone means it. 本気だ (I'm serious).

rd: じょうだん でしょ
use: Express disbelief. 冗談じゃない (this is no joke) is an angry denial.
alt: 冗談じゃない (this is no joke)

use: Slangy 'really?'. Also まじ (really). Casual only.
Brush off a question or worry. 'Nothing' as a sort of evasion.
Dismiss a feeling or sound as imagined. Often in horror scenes.
alt: 気のせいだよ (it's just in your head)
気のせいかな (maybe it's my imagination)

use: Something self-evident. 当たり前だ! 'Of course!'
Declare something impossible or refuse. Polite: 無理です. 無理しないで means 'don't push yourself'.
alt: 無理しないで (don't overdo it)

use: Alert to an emergency or grumbling about difficulty. Polite: 大変です. 大変でしたね is sympathy.
alt: 大変だったね (that was rough)

use: Rough command. Gentler: 離して.
Challenge in a fight, or calling someone near. Rough and masculine.

rd: おまえ は だれ だ
lit: お前 (you, rough) は (topic) 誰 (who) だ (is)
use: Confrontational question to a stranger. お前 is rude. Polite: あなたは誰ですか.

rd: おれ に まかせろ
lit: 俺 (I, rough male) に (to) 任せろ (entrust, command)
use: Confident hero line, masculine. Neutral version: 私に任せて.

rd: いっしょ に いこう
lit: 一緒に (together) 行こう (let's go)
use: Invitation to join forces. Polite: 一緒に行きましょう.
Relief when something works out or someone is safe. Polite: よかったです.
alt: 無事でよかった (glad you're safe)

use: Relief of arriving or finishing before it was too late. Opposite 間に合わなかった.
alt: 間に合わなかった (didn't make it)

lit: あきらめ (give up) ない (not)
use: Hero determination; also a motto. Command: あきらめるな (don't give up).
alt: あきらめるな (don't give up)

rd: なに を いっている
lit: 何 (what) を (object) 言って (say) いる (is doing)
use: Incredulous reaction. Casual: 何言ってるの. Rough: 何を言ってやがる.
alt: 何を言っているんですか (polite)

rd: ほんとうに ごめん
use: Sincere apology to a friend or family member. More polite: 本当にすみません.
alt: 本当にごめんなさい (more polite)

use: Thanks for a rescue or favour. Polite: 助かりました.
alt: ありがとう、助かった (thanks, you saved me)

rd: いいかげん に しろ
lit: いい加減 (decent limit) に (to) しろ (do, command)
use: Angry demand to stop. Heard when someone has had enough. Rough.
alt: いい加減にして (a bit softer)
いい加減にしてください (polite)

rd: しんぱい する な
use: Reassurance, masculine. Neutral: 心配しないで.
alt: 心配しないでください (polite)

lit: 気 (attention) を (object) つけろ (attach, command)
use: Warning to take care. Neutral: 気をつけて.

rd: やる しか ない
en: There's no choice but to do it
lit: やる (do) しか (nothing but) ない (none)
use: A resolved moment before a hard act. Polite: やるしかありません.
Casual line when arriving or when ready. Hero shows up: お待たせ!
Rough way to call someone, used by men or in anger. Do not use to people you respect.
Get someone's attention among friends or family. Friendlier than おい.
Accusation in drama, or playful. 嘘つき! is a cry in betrayals.
Sharp question to an unknown person, often in the dark. Rough and masculine.
Urging someone onward. Often cheering a hero on.
Pledge of protection, a trope: 俺が守る (I'll protect you). Dictionary form used as declaration.
alt: 守ってみせる (I'll protect you, I swear)

use: Shows that things turned out as you thought. Casual form of やはり.
alt: やっぱりね (just as I thought)

use: Praise for someone living up to reputation: さすがだね.
Emotional plea. Polite: お願いします.
alt: お願いだから (I'm begging you)
